newsitem.title: USA: Andersen Worldwide defers naming permanent CEO.
newsitem.headline: Andersen Worldwide defers naming permanent CEO.

text.p: Andersen Worldwide said Monday it named W. Robert Grafton acting chief executive to serve after the term of the current chief executive, Lawrence Weinbach, ends on August 31.
Andersen also said it has deferred naming a permanent chief executive.
Grafton is currently Andersen's chairman of the board of partners.
Andersen said it will convene a "high-level group" to address organizational issues before it names a permanent managing partner and chief executive.
The group will develop specific proposals for addressing organizational issues by spring 1998, the company said in a statement.

On Friday, the Wall Street Journal reported that the latest nominee to head Andersen failed to secure enough partner votes to take the post, the second time in less than two months that the board's choice to succeed Weinbach was rejected.
In its statement, Andersen said its partners confirmed at its recent global meeting its preference to keep the organization together by making "appropriate internal adjustments."
Grafton will keep his position as chairman when he becomes acting CEO, a company spokesman said.
